----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                           *vllm.models.hy_v4*

HY V4 (`hy_v4`) model --- hardware-isolated entry point.

HY V4 combines three architectural pieces:

- iHC (independent Hyper-Connections): the single residual stream is
  replaced by `hc_mult` parallel residual channels, gated per sub-block.
- MLA + lightning indexer: multi-head latent attention with an optional
  DSA-style sparse top-k selection, plus an output gate and a learnable
  sink.
- MoE: sigmoid-routed experts with a clamped SwiGLU and shared experts.

The package is organized like `vllm.models.deepseek_v32`: this module is the
only public entry point and dispatches on the current platform, so registry
entries never reach into a platform subpackage.

NVIDIA and ROCm are supported, the latter through `amd/`. The port also
drops the reference implementation's HPC/TPCP fusion paths, which depend on
infrastructure that does not exist in this tree.

Modules: ~

- `amd` --
- `dfly_config` --
- `nvidia` --

Classes: ~

- `HYV4MTP` -- HY V4 MTP draft head.
- `HYV4VLForConditionalGeneration` -- HYV4 VL composition using the
  platform-selected HYV4 text model.

matching `DeepseekV32MTP` / `KimiK3MTP` / `HYV3MTP`.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                            *vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.loop*

Looped Inkling2 checkpoints (`loop_config`).

The core layers `[core_start, core_end)` run `num_passes` times: a prelude,
then each pass from the AttnRes state after the prelude, then the coda from
the last pass's state. Each pass of a core layer has its own KV and
conv-state caches. In passes after the first, every core sublayer input
(attention q/k/v and MLP) is blended with a message: a normalized-value
AttnRes read of the previous pass's blocks, merged by a gated low-rank
controller. Each sublayer's short conv runs fused with the next AttnRes mix
(and small batches at TP > 1 with its all-reduce); without sequence
parallel.

Classes: ~

- `Inkling2LoopDecoderLayer` -- A loop core layer: per-pass caches and a
  message controller per
- `Inkling2LoopForConditionalGeneration` -- The inkling2_loop checkpoints'
  architecture name; the model is
- `Inkling2LoopModel` --
- `Inkling2MessageController` -- Blends a loop message into a core sublayer
  input: from the rank-r

                   *vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.loop.Inkling2LoopDecoderLayer*
`Inkling2LoopDecoderLayer`

Bases: `Inkling2DecoderLayer`

A loop core layer: per-pass caches and a message controller per stream
(`LOOP_STREAMS`), whose weights are stacked over the streams.

Methods: ~

- `blend` -- The streams controllers on fp32 (S, T, D) dest (may

             *vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.loop.Inkling2LoopDecoderLayer.blend*
`blend(streams, dest, message, norm_weight, norm_eps)`

The `streams` controllers on fp32 `(S, T, D)` `dest` (may broadcast over
streams) and `message`, each output RMS-normalized with its row of
`norm_weight` `(S, D)`: bf16 `(S, T, D)`.

                  *vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.loop.Inkling2MessageController*
`Inkling2MessageController`

Bases: `Module`

Blends a loop message into a core sublayer input: from the rank-`r`
projection `h` of the RMS-normalized `[dest, message]`,
`(1 - tanh(forget(h))) * dest + tanh(gain(h)) * message` in fp32.

The weights are views of the layer's stream-stacked weights
(`Inkling2LoopDecoderLayer`), which run every stream at once; `forward` is
the per-stream reference.

Methods: ~

- `forward` -- fp32 (T, D) dest and message -> fp32 (T, D).

          *vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.loop.Inkling2MessageController.forward*
`forward(dest, message)`

fp32 `(T, D)` `dest` and `message` -> fp32 `(T, D)`.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                           *vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.sconv*

Inkling2 short convolutions with their state kept in a sliding-window cache.

Each decoder layer owns one `InklingConvState` (shared with Inkling v1)
holding its four conv streams (K, V, attn-out, mlp-out) packed head-major.
K/V are TP-sharded with the KV heads; the attn-/mlp-output streams are
replicated full-width on every rank (`replicate_hidden=True`).

Classes: ~

- `Inkling2ShortConv` -- Causal depthwise conv (+ residual, scaled) over one
  conv-state stream.

`Inkling2ShortConv`      *vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.sconv.Inkling2ShortConv*

Bases: `Module`

Causal depthwise conv (+ residual, scaled) over one conv-state stream.

Static: `weight` of shape `(dim, 1, W)`. Dynamic: per-token taps
`static_w (W, dim) + weight_proj(dynamic_input)` per head. The K/V convs
only hold weights; the attention prologue kernel runs both.

                *vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.sconv.Inkling2ShortConv.conv_mix*

    residual=None, sp=None, halo=0, prefix_align=0, owner=None)`

`KimiK3DSAIndexer`              *vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.dsa.KimiK3DSAIndexer*

Bases: `Module`

wq/wk/wv indexer projections with FP8 or MXFP4 scoring on ROCm.

Forward quantizes the indexer query, folds the scales into the per-head
weights and drives `torch.ops.vllm.rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer` via
`SparseAttnIndexer.forward_hip` with `cache_layout="NORMAL"`: the indexer
pages are block-flat, which the Triton insert wrapper cannot infer from the
cache shape alone. MXFP4 uses group scales and dedicated FlyDSL scoring with
the same global token-index output contract.

  *vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.dsa.KimiK3DSAIndexer._quantize_index_q_and_weights*

Fold the query, head-count and softmax scales into FP32 weights, preserving
the projection dtype's intermediate rounding.

`KimiK3DSAIndexerKNorm`    *vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.dsa.KimiK3DSAIndexerKNorm*

Bases: `Module`

Bias-full fp32 LayerNorm for the DSA indexer shared key.

weight/bias load and stay in fp32; a copy in the activation dtype is cached
so the fp32 round trip does not cost two casts per call. F.layer_norm still
accumulates in fp32 for a bf16 input, so the only numeric change is that
weight/bias multiply in the activation dtype.

*vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.mla.KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper._compute_w_fold*
`_compute_w_fold(w_qb, w_uk, num_heads, qk_nope_head_dim, qk_rope_head_dim)`
`staticmethod`

W_fold = [W_UK @ W_qb_nope ; W_qb_pe]: one GEMM gives [ql_nope | q_pe].

`w_qb` is the q_b_proj weight [N * (P + R), Lq], `w_uk` is [L, N, P]. Rows
hold all heads' nope rows, then all pe rows, so the two output halves of
`x @ W_fold.T` are contiguous: [B, N * L] and [B, N * R].

*vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.mla.KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper._fused_decode*
`_fused_decode(q, kv_c_normed, k_pe, output_shape, attn_metadata, layer,
    kv_cache, slot_mapping)`

Decode-only MLA through one fused AITER launch.

Replaces the fp8 KV-cache write plus the `[ql_nope | q_pe]` concat and that
query's static fp8 quant with a single `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla`.
On an untouched upstream build the concat and quant already arrive as one
inductor-fused kernel, so this collapses two launches into one.

                                            *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model*

Inference-only MiniMax M3 (text backbone) model --- AMD ROCm implementation.

Self-contained per-platform impl (mirrors `deepseek_v4/amd`). It is
identical to `../nvidia/model.py` except for RMS normalization: FlashInfer's
Gemma RMSNorm kernels are CUDA-only, so `MiniMAXGemmaRMSNorm` here uses a
native (FlashInfer-free) implementation.

  The MiniMax-M3-preview config selects a single set of branches: ~

  - qk_norm_type == "per_head"
  - SwiGLU-OAI MLPs (Transformers reports hidden_act as "silu")
  - use_gemma_norm == True -> Gemma-style RMSNorm everywhere
  - attention_output_gate == False
  - scoring_func == "sigmoid" with a routing-bias correction term
  - "minimax_m3_sparse" layer_types -> a subset of layers run the extra
    "index" attention branch.

`MiniMAXGemmaRMSNorm`   *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model.MiniMAXGemmaRMSNorm*

Bases: `Module`

Gemma-style RMS normalization (native ROCm implementation).

Normalizes in fp32 and scales by `(1 + weight)` --- numerically equivalent
to the FlashInfer `gemma_rmsnorm` / `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` kernels used
in the NVIDIA path, which are unavailable on ROCm. When `residual` is given,
the fused add + norm returns the updated `(normed, residual)` pair.

The fp32 normalize + scale + (optional) residual-add run in a single fused
Triton pass (`amd.ops.gemma_rmsnorm` / `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm`) instead of
a chain of elementwise PyTorch kernels.

                   *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model.MiniMaxM3SparseAttention*
`MiniMaxM3SparseAttention`

Bases: `Module`, `AttentionLayerBase`

Block-sparse attention layer with the lightning-indexer branch.

This is a merged attention layer: it owns the projections (qkv + index q/k),
per-head QK norms and RoPE, and the attention-backend wiring that a generic
`Attention` layer would normally provide --- it binds the
`MiniMaxM3SparseBackend` + main impl, registers the main paged K/V cache,
and owns the lightning indexer (`MiniMaxM3Indexer`), which holds the
index-key side cache.

The index branch (index_{q,k}proj + index_norm) feeds the sparse top-k block
selection. M3 always disables the index value/output projections
(`sparse_disable_index_value` set for every sparse layer), so
`index_{v,o}_proj` are never created.

*vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model.MiniMaxM3SparseAttention._emits_o_proj_mxfp8*
`_emits_o_proj_mxfp8()`

Whether this step's attention writes MXFP8 for `o_proj` itself: the NVFP4
decode kernel can, `o_proj` takes MXFP8 input, and the batch is decode-only
(a captured piecewise graph or a mixed batch keeps the bf16 output).

    *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._aiter_moe_fused_shared_experts_enabled*
`_aiter_moe_fused_shared_experts_enabled(is_fused_shared_expert_enabled)`

Whether the fused shared expert routes through aiter's grouped top-k MoE.

A strict sub-case of `is_fused_shared_expert_enabled`: shared-expert fusion
must already be opted in (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS`) and
allowed (not under expert parallelism). When additionally on gfx950 with an
active aiter MoE backend, the shared expert is appended inside aiter's
biased grouped top-k kernel (`num_fused_shared_experts`) instead of the vLLM
router's torch concat. Otherwise FSE still runs via the vLLM top-k bias
router.

                          *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._build_rotary_emb*
`_build_rotary_emb(config, head_dim)`

Build the (partial NeoX) RoPE from `config.rope_parameters`.

Without scaling the cos/sin cache is sized to `max_position_embeddings`
(524288 native); a request whose positions exceed that reads the cache out
of bounds and the worker hard-crashes (no Python traceback). When scaling is
set (e.g. YaRN `factor: 2` to reach 1M), it is threaded into `get_rope` so
the proper scaled embedding is built and its cache covers
`original_max_position_embeddings * factor` positions. Default behavior (no
scaling) is unchanged. Shared by the dense and sparse attention layers, and
the index branch reuses the returned module.

Note: for the VL checkpoint, set the scaling on the text config
(`--hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"rope_parameters":{...}}}'`) -- that is
the config the decoder reads here; a top-level override does not reach it.

                 *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8*
`_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8(qkv_proj)`

Whether `input_layernorm` can hand `qkv_proj` an MXFP8 activation.

The quant key does not encode the scale layout (FlashInfer wants swizzled
scales under the same key), so this also requires a ROCm kernel that reads
the row-major scales the fused norm writes.

                              *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._is_moe_layer*
`_is_moe_layer(config, layer_id)`

Whether this layer's MLP is a sparse MoE block (vs a dense MLP).

`_kv_insert_operand(t)`  *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._kv_insert_operand*

K or V operand for `aiter.reshape_and_cache`, without a needless copy.

The AITER sparse-PA insert takes K and V as column slices of the fused
`[q | k | v | index_q | index_k]` projection, so they are row-strided views
and never contiguous. `reshape_and_cache` does not need them to be: it
passes `key.stride(0)` to the kernel as the row pitch and reads
`key[token_idx * key_stride + i]` for `i` over `num_heads * head_size`, so
the only requirement is that the trailing `(num_heads, head_size)` block be
contiguous within a row, which such a slice always satisfies. Any other
layout falls back to a copy.

                       *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._mxfp8_linear_kernel*
`_mxfp8_linear_kernel(linear)`

The MXFP8 kernel of `linear`, or None.

             *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._redirect_fused_shared_experts*
`_redirect_fused_shared_experts(weights, model)`

Load fused shared experts into the routed slot after the local experts.

                    *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._should_skip_index_topk*
`_should_skip_index_topk(config, layer_id)`

ATOM `index_topk_freq` (cross-layer index sharing).

Only 1 of every `index_topk_freq` sparse-attention layers recomputes the
lightning-indexer top-k block selection; the rest reuse the selection the
preceding compute layer wrote into the shared `topk_indices_buffer` this
same forward pass. This cuts the indexer score + top-k cost ~`freq`x but
approximates the per-layer selection, so validate accuracy on long-context
inputs. Gated by `use_index_cache` in the text config; enable via
`--hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 4}}'`.

                *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._sparse_attention_layer_ids*
`_sparse_attention_layer_ids(config)`

Layer ids whose attention runs the extra sparse "index" branch.

           *vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model._sparse_attention_layer_ordinals*
`_sparse_attention_layer_ordinals(config)`

Map each sparse-attention layer id to its ordinal among sparse layers.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                      *vllm.models.muse_spark*

Muse Spark HF model entry point.

The model classes load on first access, so importing a submodule such as
`common.vision` doesn't import the NVIDIA model. Its kernels import
FlashInfer, which queries the GPU at import and so initializes CUDA in the
importing process; processes forked from it afterwards can't use CUDA.

Modules: ~

- `amd` -- AMD ROCm implementation of Muse Spark.
- `common` -- Platform-independent MuseSpark preprocessing.
- `nvidia` -- NVIDIA-specific MuseSpark model implementations.

Classes: ~

  output-distribution transform.
- `MuseSparkForConditionalGeneration` -- Muse Spark Omni: text stack plus
  NaViT vision and waveform audio.

                           *vllm.models.muse_spark.MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM*
`MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM`

Bases: `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM`

Muse DSpark head with the target's output-distribution transform.

Methods: ~

  apply_output_logit_transform.
- `sample_markov_chain` -- Fuse sampling tails after the ordinary
  base-logits projection.

  *vllm.models.muse_spark.MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM._sample_sequential_fused*
`_sample_sequential_fused(speculator, num_reqs, head_hidden)`

The `sample_sequential` hook under the specialized decode, which
DSparkSpeculator._sample_sequential asks first: the fused Markov sampling
loop samples the drafts, and this returns True.

*vllm.models.muse_spark.MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM.output_logit_transform_params*
`output_logit_transform_params()`

`(multiplier, soft_cap)` of `apply_output_logit_transform`.

The fused DSpark Markov loop computes the transform from these values
(`logits * multiplier`, then `soft_cap * tanh(x / soft_cap)` unless
`soft_cap` is None) instead of calling it, so a subclass that changes the
transform must override this too.

       *vllm.models.muse_spark.MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM.sample_markov_chain*
`sample_markov_chain(speculator, base_logits, prev, idx_map, sample_pos,
    out_tokens, *, prev_indices=None)`

Fuse sampling tails after the ordinary base-logits projection. Returns each
step's Markov embedding, `[rows, steps, rank]`, or None when the speculator
must run its own loop.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                         *vllm.models.qwen3_5*

Qwen3.5 model --- hardware-isolated entry point.

The NVIDIA and ROCm variants use the eager + breakable CUDA-graph modelling
code with explicit fused kernels. XPU uses a separate eager + breakable
XPU-graph implementation with explicit routed/shared expert fusion for
eligible MoE calls. All other platforms keep the previous torch.compile
implementation in `vllm/model_executor/models/` so their behavior is
unchanged.

  to a batch.
- `positions` (Tensor) -- Flattened (concatenated) position ids
  corresponding to a batch. NOTE: If mrope is enabled (default setting for
  Qwen3VL opensource models), the shape will be (3, seq_len), otherwise it
  will be (seq_len,).
- `intermediate_tensors` (IntermediateTensors | None, default: None ) --
  Intermediate tensors from previous pipeline stages.
- `inputs_embeds` (Tensor | None, default: None ) -- Pre-computed input
  embeddings.
- `**kwargs` (object, default: {} ) -- Additional keyword arguments
  including: - pixel_values: Pixel values to be fed to a model. None if no
  images are passed. - image_grid_thw: Tensor (n_images, 3) of image 3D grid
  in LLM. None if no images are passed. - pixel_values_videos: Pixel values
  of videos to be fed to a model. None if no videos are passed. -
  video_grid_thw: Tensor (n_videos, 3) of video 3D grid in LLM. None if no
  videos are passed.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                   *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.hyperconnection*

HyperConnection (Gated Residual) utilities for the AMD model variant.

Implements the HyperConnection residual scheme proposed in
"HyperConnections" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19606). This AMD variant
delays each HC combine to the following HC mix boundary. HC glue kernels,
including fused combine+RMSNorm, live in `ops/hc.py`; projections remain
standard vLLM Linear modules.

Hidden states between layers have shape `[..., HC*HS]` with HS inner (HC
outer, HS inner --- checkpoint-native layout).

Typical usage inside a transformer decoder layer:

>python
    self.attn_hc = GatedResidual(hc_config)

    hidden_states, block_input, injection = self.attn_hc.mix(hidden_states)
    attention_output = attention(block_input)
    hidden_states, block_input, injection = self.mlp_hc.combine_and_mix(
        hidden_states, attention_output, injection
    )
<
Classes: ~

- `GatedResidual` -- Gated HyperConnection with learnable low-rank mixing
  and injection.
- `HyperConnectionConfig` -- Configuration shared by all HyperConnection
  variants.

`GatedResidual`      *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.hyperconnection.GatedResidual*

Bases: `Module`

Gated HyperConnection with learnable low-rank mixing and injection.

`combine_and_mix()` runs the pre pipeline (grouped GemmaRMSNorm -> merged
low-rank down+inject GEMM -> silu -> up GEMM -> sigmoid -> gated mean over
the HC streams). When passed a pending block output and an injection, it
fuses their residual combine with the RMSNorm. Final mixers use
`use_combine=False` and do not produce a new injection.

Weights: the norm owns the grouped GemmaRMSNorm affine; the projections are
vLLM Linear modules (merged replicated linear for down+inject), so GEMM
dispatch (e.g. the low-latency skinny GEMM) applies through the standard
quant_method mechanism.

Methods: ~

- `combine_and_mix` -- Consume a pending combine, then prepare the next
  block input.

     *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.hyperconnection.GatedResidual.combine_and_mix*
`combine_and_mix(hidden_states, prev_block_output, prev_injection)`

Consume a pending combine, then prepare the next block input.

`hidden_states` is the multi-stream state from before the pending block's
mix. Its combine with `block_output` is fused with this module's input
RMSNorm.

             *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.hyperconnection.HyperConnectionConfig*
`HyperConnectionConfig` `dataclass`

Configuration shared by all HyperConnection variants.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                               *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.mtp*

Inference-only Qwen4Exp MTP (Multi-Token Predictor) model.

The MTP draft model reuses the Qwen4Exp backbone (PLE/HC/MoE) but: - drops
all multi-modal handling (text-only), - forces PLE off while keeping the
main model's HC stream count, - fuses the backbone hidden and the new-token
embedding via `residual_linear_shared` (fc_embedding + shared fc_hidden)
instead of the `Linear(2H, H)` + repeat used by other MTP variants, - emits
TWO hidden streams per step (scheme A): a single stream [T, H] (final-mixer
collapsed, fed to the LM head) and a pre-final-mixer multi stream [T,
hc_count*H] (fed to the next draft step).

`QSAIndexer`                        *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.qsa.QSAIndexer*

Bases: `Module`

Replicated Q/K projection plus paged, weight-free QSA selection.

`prefix` must be the checkpoint's indexer prefix, normally
`model.layers.N.self_attn.indexer`. Consequently the trainable names are
`index_qk_proj`, `q_layernorm` and `k_layernorm` under that prefix.

Methods: ~

- `forward` -- Return fixed-width request-relative token indices padded with
  -1.
- `normalize_compressed_keys` -- Normalize pooled K and apply the first
  token's exact group position.
- `project` -- Project replicated Q/K and split, leaving both operands
  unrotated.
- `project_qk` -- Project replicated Q/K, normalize+rotate Q, and preserve
  raw K.

                     *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.qsa.QSAIndexer._fused_prepare*
`_fused_prepare(projected_q, raw_keys, positions, raw_metadata,
    compressed_metadata, attn, qkv, slot_mapping, gate_out)`

Prepare the indexer and `attn`'s main attention in one launch.

Normalizes and rotates the index Q, compresses K and writes both side
caches, which replaces `project_qk`'s norm/RoPE half and the whole of
`_update_and_compress`. The same launch applies `attn`'s QK-norm and RoPE,
copies its gate and writes its K/V into `attn.kv_cache`, replacing
`_project_qkv_gate` and `do_kv_cache_update`. Both halves must stay
numerically interchangeable with what they replace.

                            *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.qsa.QSAIndexer.forward*
`forward(hidden_states, positions, out=None, *, attn, qkv=None,
    slot_mapping=None, gate_out=None)`

Return fixed-width request-relative token indices padded with `-1`.

With `attn.use_fused_qsa_prepare`, the same launch also writes `attn`'s K/V
into `attn.kv_cache` at `slot_mapping` and prepares its Q and gate from
`qkv`, returned as the second element (None otherwise). The gate is written
into `gate_out` when given. `qkv`, `slot_mapping` and `gate_out` are only
read in that mode.

          *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.qsa.QSAIndexer.normalize_compressed_keys*
`normalize_compressed_keys(compressed_keys, first_rope_positions)`

Normalize pooled K and apply the first token's exact group position.

                         *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.amd.qsa.QSAIndexer.project_qk*

                                                *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.common*

Common Qwen4Exp model components.

Modules: ~

- `hyperconnection` -- HyperConnection (Gated Residual) utilities.
- `ngram_embedding` -- Shared Qwen4Exp n-gram embedding storage with device
  and pinned-host backends.
- `ops` -- Qwen4Exp kernels shared by the NVIDIA and AMD backends; import
  leaf modules
- `ple` -- Common Qwen4Exp PLE helpers.
- `qsa` -- Main-attention metadata shared by the QSA platform

`GatedResidual`                   *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.common.GatedResidual*

Bases: `HyperConnectionBase`

Gated HyperConnection with learnable low-rank mixing and injection.

`mix()` applies GemmaRMSNorm per HC stream and projects through a low-rank
sigmoid gate to produce a single block input. `combine()` injects the block
output back into each stream through a learned per-stream injection weight.

This implementation uses only PyTorch operators. Tensor-parallel collectives
are supplied by its caller.

Methods: ~

- `mix` -- Mix: RMSNorm -> low-rank gate -> gated mean.

`mix(hyper_input)`            *vllm.models.qwen4_exp.common.GatedResidual.mix*

Mix: RMSNorm -> low-rank gate -> gated mean.

Bases: `Module`

parallel streams, averages them for the block input, and broadcasts the
block output back to every stream.

`Step5SparseIndexer`          *vllm.models.step5.amd.model.Step5SparseIndexer*

Bases: `Module`

MQA indexer with `heads_per_group` query heads per KV group.

Q and W are sharded like the attention KV heads, so each rank computes only
its own groups; the shared single-head K and Z stay replicated.

Methods: ~

- `forward` -- Returns `(q [T, G, 8, P] fp8, k [T, 1, P], z [T, 1, P],

                      *vllm.models.step5.amd.model.Step5SparseIndexer.forward*
`forward(hidden_states, positions, decode=None)`

Returns `(q [T, G, 8, P] fp8, k [T, 1, P], z [T, 1, P], w [T, G, 8])` for
this rank's `G` local groups, heads padded to 8.

With `decode=(summary cache, ring, slots)` it also stores each token's
open-region row and summarizes the regions it closes.

                                      *vllm.multimodal.audio.find_split_point*
`find_split_point(wav, start_idx, end_idx, min_energy_window)`

Find the best point to split audio by looking for silence or low amplitude.

Searches for the quietest region within a specified range by calculating RMS
energy in sliding windows.

Parameters: ~

- `wav` (ndarray) -- 1D mono audio array.
- `start_idx` (int) -- Start index of search region (inclusive).
- `end_idx` (int) -- End index of search region (exclusive).
- `min_energy_window` (int) -- Window size in samples for energy
  calculation.

Returns: ~

- `int` -- Index of the quietest point within the search region. This is the
- `int` -- recommended split point to minimize audio artifacts.

  Example: ~

        audio = np.random.randn(32000)

        Insert quiet region *vllm.multimodal.audio.find_split_point--insert-quiet-region*

        audio[16000:17600] = 0.01 split_idx = find_split_point( ...
        wav=audio, ... start_idx=0, ... end_idx=32000, ...
        min_energy_window=1600, ... ) 16000 <= split_idx <= 17600 True

                             *vllm.multimodal.audio.resample_audio_torchaudio*
`resample_audio_torchaudio(audio, *, orig_sr, target_sr)`

Resample audio using torchaudio's bandlimited sinc interpolation.

Unlike the PyAV resampler, this handles any input length without padding and
applies the kernel over the trailing axis, so 2D `(channels, samples)` input
needs no per-channel loop.

Parameters: ~

- `audio` (NDArray[floating]) -- Input audio. Can be: - 1D array (samples,):
  mono audio - 2D array (channels, samples): stereo audio
- `orig_sr` (float) -- Original sample rate in Hz.
- `target_sr` (float) -- Target sample rate in Hz.

Returns: ~

- `NDArray[floating]` -- Resampled audio with the same shape as the input
  (1D → 1D, 2D → 2D).

                                           *vllm.multimodal.audio.split_audio*
`split_audio(audio_data, sample_rate, max_clip_duration_s,
    overlap_duration_s, min_energy_window_size)`

Split audio into chunks with intelligent split points.

Splits long audio into smaller chunks at low-energy regions to minimize
cutting through speech. Uses overlapping windows to find quiet moments for
splitting.

Parameters: ~

- `audio_data` (ndarray) -- 1D mono audio array to split. ASR models consume
  mono, so callers must downmix before chunking.
- `sample_rate` (int) -- Sample rate of the audio in Hz.
- `max_clip_duration_s` (float) -- Maximum duration of each chunk in
  seconds.
- `overlap_duration_s` (float) -- Overlap duration in seconds between
  consecutive chunks. Used to search for optimal split points.
- `min_energy_window_size` (int) -- Window size in samples for finding
  low-energy regions.

Returns: ~

- `list[ndarray]` -- List of 1D audio chunks.

Raises: ~

- `AssertionError` -- If audio_data is not 1D.

  Example: ~

        audio = np.random.randn(1040000) # 65 seconds at 16kHz chunks =
        split_audio( ... audio_data=audio, ... sample_rate=16000, ...
        max_clip_duration_s=30.0, ... overlap_duration_s=1.0, ...
        min_energy_window_size=1600, ... ) len(chunks) 3

  item itself. This is optional and may not be needed by some cache
  implementations.

                         *vllm.multimodal.cache.LruKeyReplicatedReceiverCache*
`LruKeyReplicatedReceiverCache`

Bases: `BaseMultiModalReceiverCache`

The cache which is used on P1 when LRU caching is enabled.

How to update each item:

- If the caller sent tensor data, store it (replacing any cached item under
  the same key) and return that data. P0 can miss after independent LRU
  eviction and resend a different item for the same identity.
- If the caller sent no data and the item is cached, return the cached item.
- If the caller sent no data and the item is not cached, raise
  `MultiModalCacheMissError`.

                           *vllm.multimodal.cache.LruKeyReplicatedSenderCache*
`LruKeyReplicatedSenderCache`

Bases: `BaseMultiModalProcessorCache`

The cache which is used on P0 when LRU caching is enabled.

How to update each item:

- If the item is already in the cache, clear the input to avoid unnecessary
  IPC.
- If the item is not in the cache, store the metadata of that item so that
  the eviction policy remains the same as the cache on P1, and return the
  input. By only storing the metadata, we avoid keeping the data itself in
  memory inside P0.

`MultiModalCacheMissError`    *vllm.multimodal.cache.MultiModalCacheMissError*

Bases: `RuntimeError`

Raised by the P1 receiver cache when items are requested with no data and
are not cached.

P0 (frontend) keeps a metadata-only shadow of P1 (engine) and sends
`data=None` on a shadow hit. The two caches are updated in different orders
across processes, so they can drift -- leaving P0 referencing items P1 has
evicted. Raising (instead of asserting) lets the engine return a retryable
response and have P0 drop the stale entries
(`BaseMultiModalProcessorCache.invalidate`) so the client resends the data.
Carries every drifted `mm_hash` in the request so P0 can drop them all in
one pass -- one retry then recovers the whole request, not one item per
retry.

                          *vllm.multimodal.cache.MultiModalProcessorOnlyCache*
`MultiModalProcessorOnlyCache`

Bases: `BaseMultiModalProcessorCache`

The cache which is used on P0 when IPC caching is disabled.

How to update each item:

- If the item is in the cache, replace the input with the cached item.
- If the item is not in the cache, store that item (which includes tensor
  data and metadata) into the cache, and return the input.

                           *vllm.multimodal.cache.ShmObjectStoreReceiverCache*
`ShmObjectStoreReceiverCache`

Bases: `BaseMultiModalReceiverCache`

The cache which is used on P1 Worker Process when SHM caching is enabled.

How to update each item:

- If the item has an address, replace the input with the cached item.
- If not, return the input.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                              *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory*

Admission control for frontend GPU-side multimodal work.

When multimodal media is decoded on the GPU in the API-server (frontend)
process, the decoded buffers compete for the same device memory that the
engine reserves for weights, activations, and the KV cache. To keep the
frontend's GPU usage within a sequestered budget (see
`MultiModalConfig.mm_ipc_gpu_memory_gb`), decode paths acquire the number of
bytes they need from a process-global `MultiModalGPUMemoryPool` before
allocating on the device and release them once the device memory is freed.

The pool is a simple byte-counting semaphore: `acquire` blocks until enough
budget is free, so concurrent requests serialize rather than oversubscribe
the GPU. It lives only in the frontend process; the engine carves the
matching amount out of its KV-cache budget so the headroom physically
exists.

Classes: ~

- `MultiModalGPUMemoryLease` -- A handle for bytes acquired from a
  MultiModalGPUMemoryPool.
- `MultiModalGPUMemoryPool` -- Blocking byte-counting semaphore for frontend
  GPU multimodal memory.

Functions: ~

- `get_mm_gpu_ipc_pool` -- Return the process-global pool, or None when
  gating is disabled.
- `maybe_init_mm_gpu_ipc_pool` -- Create and install the global pool from
  the configured GiB budget.
- `reserve_mm_ipc_gpu_memory` -- Return KV-cache memory remaining after
  frontend multimodal reservations.
- `set_mm_gpu_ipc_pool` -- Install the process-global pool (frontend process
  only).

                     *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.MultiModalGPUMemoryLease*
`MultiModalGPUMemoryLease`

A handle for bytes acquired from a `MultiModalGPUMemoryPool`.

Releasing is idempotent and the lease doubles as a context manager so the
budget is returned even if the decode raises.

                      *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.MultiModalGPUMemoryPool*
`MultiModalGPUMemoryPool`

Blocking byte-counting semaphore for frontend GPU multimodal memory.

Thread-safe in both directions: `acquire` (blocking) and `release` are
typically called from the renderer's multimodal executor threads.

Methods: ~

- `acquire` -- Reserve nbytes, blocking until that much budget is free.

              *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.MultiModalGPUMemoryPool.acquire*
`acquire(nbytes)`

Reserve `nbytes`, blocking until that much budget is free.

Raises `ValueError` if `nbytes` exceeds the pool's total capacity, since
such a request could never be satisfied.

`get_mm_gpu_ipc_pool()`   *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.get_mm_gpu_ipc_pool*

Return the process-global pool, or `None` when gating is disabled.

                   *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.maybe_init_mm_gpu_ipc_pool*
`maybe_init_mm_gpu_ipc_pool(mm_ipc_gpu_memory_gb, api_process_count=1)`

Create and install the global pool from the configured GiB budget.

Returns `None` (and leaves gating disabled) when the budget is 0. When
multiple API-server processes share one engine, each process gets an equal
slice of the user-provided frontend budget.

                    *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.reserve_mm_ipc_gpu_memory*
`reserve_mm_ipc_gpu_memory(available_kv_cache_memory_bytes, mm_config,
    api_process_count=1)`

Return KV-cache memory remaining after frontend multimodal reservations.

The reservation covers:

- The total `mm_ipc_gpu_memory_gb` budget for transient decoded-frame
  buffers. This budget is divided among API processes, so it is not
  multiplied by `api_process_count`.
- For GPU video backends, a fixed upper bound for each API process's
  retained decoder surfaces and CUDA context. The PyNvVideoCodec surface
  reservation scales with its configured `hw_decoders` value, and the entire
  decoder reservation scales with `api_process_count` because these
  resources are not shared between processes.

Parameters: ~

- `available_kv_cache_memory_bytes` (int) -- KV-cache capacity before
  reserving memory for frontend multimodal processing.
- `mm_config` (MultiModalConfig | None) -- Multimodal configuration, or None
  when multimodal processing is disabled.
- `api_process_count` (int, default: 1 ) -- Number of frontend API processes
  sharing the GPU. Values below one are treated as one.

Returns: ~

- `int` -- KV-cache capacity after subtracting the frontend reservation.

Raises: ~

- `ValueError` -- If the reservation leaves no memory for the KV cache.

                          *vllm.multimodal.gpu_ipc_memory.set_mm_gpu_ipc_pool*
`set_mm_gpu_ipc_pool(pool)`

Install the process-global pool (frontend process only).

is uniquely decodable and distinct inputs cannot share a key.

                 *vllm.multimodal.hasher.MultiModalHasher.iter_value_to_bytes*

`MultiModalKwargsItems`                *vllm.multimodal.MultiModalKwargsItems*

Bases: `UserDict[str, Sequence[_I]]`

A dictionary of processed multi-modal inputs by modality.

For example, given a processor that processes images into `pixel_values` and
`image_grid_thw`, and audios into `input_audio_features`, a prompt with 2
images and 1 audio will be processed into a `MultiModalKwargsItems` with the
following structure:

>python
    MultiModalKwargsItems(
        {
            "image": [
                # For the first image
                MultiModalKwargsItem({"pixel_values": ..., "image_grid_thw": ...}),
                # For the second imgae
                MultiModalKwargsItem({"pixel_values": ..., "image_grid_thw": ...}),
            ],
            "audio": [
                # For the first audio
                MultiModalKwargsItem({"input_audio_features": ...}),
            ],
        }
    )
<
Unlike HF processing which returns all items in a single dictionary with
batched keyword arguments, we split up the items because some of them may
already be cached. Also, items from multiple requests may be batched
together to improve throughput, using the logic defined by the
|vllm.multimodal.inputs.BaseMultiModalField| for each keyword argument.

Methods: ~

- `get_data` -- Construct a dictionary of keyword arguments to pass to the
  model.

                              *vllm.multimodal.MultiModalKwargsItems.get_data*
`get_data(*, device=None, pin_memory=False)`

Construct a dictionary of keyword arguments to pass to the model.

`MultiModalKwargsItems`         *vllm.multimodal.inputs.MultiModalKwargsItems*

Bases: `UserDict[str, Sequence[_I]]`

A dictionary of processed multi-modal inputs by modality.

For example, given a processor that processes images into `pixel_values` and
`image_grid_thw`, and audios into `input_audio_features`, a prompt with 2
images and 1 audio will be processed into a `MultiModalKwargsItems` with the
following structure:

>python
    MultiModalKwargsItems(
        {
            "image": [
                # For the first image
                MultiModalKwargsItem({"pixel_values": ..., "image_grid_thw": ...}),
                # For the second imgae
                MultiModalKwargsItem({"pixel_values": ..., "image_grid_thw": ...}),
            ],
            "audio": [
                # For the first audio
                MultiModalKwargsItem({"input_audio_features": ...}),
            ],
        }
    )
<
Unlike HF processing which returns all items in a single dictionary with
batched keyword arguments, we split up the items because some of them may
already be cached. Also, items from multiple requests may be batched
together to improve throughput, using the logic defined by the
|vllm.multimodal.inputs.BaseMultiModalField| for each keyword argument.

Methods: ~

- `get_data` -- Construct a dictionary of keyword arguments to pass to the
  model.

                       *vllm.multimodal.inputs.MultiModalKwargsItems.get_data*
`get_data(*, device=None, pin_memory=False)`

Construct a dictionary of keyword arguments to pass to the model.

`PlaceholderRange` `dataclass`       *vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange*

Placeholder location information for multi-modal data.

Example: Prompt: `AAAA BBBB What is in these images?`

Images A and B will have:

>text
    A: PlaceholderRange(offset=0, length=4)
    B: PlaceholderRange(offset=5, length=4)
<

  embedded region in prompt.
- `get_embeds_indices_in_range` -- Returns the starting and ending indices

Attributes: ~

  which positions
- `length` (int) -- The length of the placeholder.
- `offset` (int) -- The start index of the placeholder in the prompt.

                            *vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange.is_embed*
`is_embed = None` `class-attribute` `instance-attribute`

A boolean mask of shape `(length,)` indicating which positions between
`offset` and `offset + length` to assign embeddings to.

`length` `instance-attribute` *vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange.length*

The length of the placeholder.

`offset` `instance-attribute` *vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange.offset*

The start index of the placeholder in the prompt.

                *vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange.extract_embeds_range*
`extract_embeds_range()`

Extract the start and end indices of the embedded region in prompt.

For example, given `PlaceholderRange(offset=2, length=5)` and
`is_embed = [False, True, False, True, True]`, the output is
`[(1 + offset, 1 + offset), (3 + offset, 4 + offset)]`.

Returns: ~

- `list[tuple[int, int]]` -- A tuple (start, end) representing the start and
  end
- `list[tuple[int, int]]` -- indices (inclusive) of the embedded region.
- `list[tuple[int, int]]` -- Returns full placeholder range if is_embed is
  None.

         *vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange.get_embeds_indices_in_range*
`get_embeds_indices_in_range(start_idx, end_idx)`

Returns the starting and ending indices of the embeddings of encoder outputs
in the range of [start_idx, end_idx) in the placeholders.

For example, given: PlaceholderRange(offset=2, length=5, is_embed=[False,
True, False, True, True])

If start_idx=3 and end_idx=5, the output is (1, 3) because we want to get
the second and the third embeddings from the encoder output.

`MediaWithBytes` `dataclass`            *vllm.multimodal.media.MediaWithBytes*

Bases: `Generic[_T]`

Wrapper that couples a media object with its original encoded bytes.

This ensures the raw bytes and media object remain synchronized, preventing
cache corruption from in-place modifications.

The wrapper delegates attribute access to the underlying media object,
making it behave transparently like the wrapped type (e.g., PIL.Image).

NOTE: Currently, this wrapper is used only for the image and video
modalities.

Methods: ~

- `__array__` -- Allow np.array(obj) to return np.array(obj.media).
- `__getattr__` -- Delegate attribute access to the underlying media object.
- `__getitem__` -- Allow obj[i] to index obj.media (e.g. video tuples).
- `__iter__` -- Allow unpacking obj to unpack obj.media (e.g. video tuples).

Attributes: ~

- `io_config` (dict[str, Any] | None) -- Decode settings that altered the
  media relative to original_bytes

                              *vllm.multimodal.media.MediaWithBytes.io_config*
`io_config = None` `class-attribute` `instance-attribute`

Decode settings that altered the media relative to `original_bytes` (e.g.
`image_mode` conversion), so they participate in cache hashing.

                                    *vllm.multimodal.parse.EmbeddingFieldRole*
`EmbeddingFieldRole = Literal['values', 'metadata']` `module-attribute`

What a field of a pre-computed-embedding input carries.

`"values"` is the embedding tensor itself; `"metadata"` is a key that sizes
the prompt's placeholder range. The distinction is what lets one declaration
serve both an ordinary request (everything present) and an EC consumer
(embeddings arrive through the connector, metadata still in the request).

                                   *vllm.multimodal.parse.MultiModalUUIDItems*
`MultiModalUUIDItems = dict[str, Sequence[str | None]]` `module-attribute`

A normalized |vllm.inputs.MultiModalUUIDDict| such that each entry
corresponds to a list.

modality these items belong to. required_fields: Fields `data` must contain.
fields_factory: Builds the field config from the data. optional_fields:
Fields `data` may omit. Which fields these are is the caller's decision --
see `MultiModalDataParser.embedding_field_sets`, where a deployment that
receives embeddings through an EC connector makes the embeddings optional.
They still need a field config, since they are used whenever they are
supplied.

                 *vllm.multimodal.parse.MultiModalDataParser.embedding_fields*
`embedding_fields = {}` `class-attribute` `instance-attribute`

Per-modality field roles for pre-computed-embedding inputs.

Declared here rather than inside `_parse_*_data` so an EC producer can read
it too: on a producer the request carries real media, so the branch that
builds `DictEmbeddingItems` never runs, yet the producer still has to know
which processed keys to publish. One declaration, both sides, no drift.

*vllm.multimodal.processing.context.BaseProcessingInfo.get_mm_max_tokens_per_item*
`get_mm_max_tokens_per_item(seq_len, mm_counts)`

Return the maximum number of tokens per item of for each modality.

When `None` (the default) is returned, vLLM will generate dummy inputs
(images/videos) at maximum possible sizes and process them to determine the
maximum token count per modality.

This approach works but can be very slow for certain models (e.g.,
Qwen2.5-VL), leading to very long startup time. For better performance, each
model can override this method to return pre-computed maximum token counts,
avoiding the need for dummy input generation and processing.

  Note: ~

  The maximum number of tokens per item of each modality returned from this
  function should respect the model's maximum sequence length and the
  maximum number of items of each modality allowed, and agree with dummy
  inputs (images/videos) at maximum possible sizes.

*vllm.multimodal.processing.context.BaseProcessingInfo.get_supported_mm_limits*
`get_supported_mm_limits()`

Return the maximum supported number of items for each modality.

A value of `None` means unlimited number of items.

Omitting a modality from the returned dictionary means that it is not
supported at all.

*vllm.multimodal.processing.context.InputProcessingContext.get_merged_mm_kwargs*
`get_merged_mm_kwargs(kwargs, *, supported_mm_processor_kwargs=None)`

Merge configured and request `mm_processor_kwargs`.

When `supported_mm_processor_kwargs` is provided, flat keys are matched
against the keys supported by each HuggingFace processor kwarg scope.
Matching flat keys are routed to every scope that supports them and removed
from the shared flat namespace; keys not supported by any scope remain flat.

Without `supported_mm_processor_kwargs`, flat keys already represented in at
least one existing mapping-valued scope are removed from the shared flat
namespace; all other flat keys are left unchanged because there is no
information to determine which scopes should receive them.

             *vllm.multimodal.processing.context._resolve_mm_processor_kwargs*
`_resolve_mm_processor_kwargs(kwargs, supported_mm_processor_kwargs=None)`

Resolve flat processor kwargs into HuggingFace processor kwarg scopes.

With `supported_mm_processor_kwargs`, each scope lists the flat keys it
supports. Matching flat keys are routed to every scope that supports them,
existing scoped values take precedence, and keys not supported by any scope
remain flat.

Without `supported_mm_processor_kwargs`, flat keys already represented in at
least one existing mapping-valued scope are removed from the shared flat
namespace; all other flat keys are left unchanged because there is no
information to determine which scopes should receive them.

 *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseMultiModalProcessor._apply_hf_processor_main*

*vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseMultiModalProcessor._apply_prompt_updates_via_text*
`_apply_prompt_updates_via_text(token_ids, mm_prompt_updates, *,
    encode_segments_separately=False)`

Apply multi-modal prompt updates in text space, then encode the result.

A non-special-token target may be tokenized differently inside the prompt
because the tokens may go across the boundaries of the target (e.g. when
searching for "foo" in "food", if "food" itself makes up a token, then the
token ID of "foo" will not appear at all). Since it is inefficient to search
for all possible tokenizations of the target in the prompt, we instead
perform text-based updates on the decoded token IDs, then encode them back.

`_get_prompt_updates(mm_items, hf_processor_mm_kwargs, out_mm_kwargs)`
`abstractmethod`

Given the original multi-modal items for this modality and HF-processed
data, output the updates to perform.

The information returned by this method is used to update token inputs which
bypass the HF processor. It is also used to update the output of HF
processor if the HF process does not apply prompt updates to text inputs.

Moreover, this information is critical to determine the token positions in
order to construct |vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange| for each
multi-modal item.

       *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseMultiModalProcessor._iter_text_matches*

  *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseMultiModalProcessor._postprocess_hf_mm_data*

Post-process the combined processor and passthrough data.

By default, the output is returned as-is. If you need to modify the output
of the HF processor before it is converted into multi-modal keyword
arguments, you should override this method.

      *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseMultiModalProcessor._postprocess_prompt*
`_postprocess_prompt(prompt)`

Post-process the prompt token IDs before locating or applying multi-modal
prompt updates.

By default, the prompt is returned as-is. If the HF processor (or chat
template) applies additional transformations to the prompt that are not
reflected in its multi-modal outputs, you should override this method to
replicate them.

                    *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseMultiModalProcessor.apply*
`apply(inputs, timing_ctx)`

Process multi-modal inputs to be used in vLLM.

The main steps are:

1. Perform MM-specific post-processing to the token inputs.
2. Apply HF Processor on multi-modal data together with optional dummy text,
   outputting processed multi-modal data tensors.
3. Find and update sequences in the token IDs with placeholder tokens. The
   number of placeholder tokens equals the feature size of the multi-modal
   data outputted by the multi-modal encoder.
4. Extract information about the placeholder tokens from the processed token
   IDs.

    *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseProcessingInfo.get_mm_max_tokens_per_item*
`get_mm_max_tokens_per_item(seq_len, mm_counts)`

Return the maximum number of tokens per item of for each modality.

When `None` (the default) is returned, vLLM will generate dummy inputs
(images/videos) at maximum possible sizes and process them to determine the
maximum token count per modality.

This approach works but can be very slow for certain models (e.g.,
Qwen2.5-VL), leading to very long startup time. For better performance, each
model can override this method to return pre-computed maximum token counts,
avoiding the need for dummy input generation and processing.

  Note: ~

  The maximum number of tokens per item of each modality returned from this
  function should respect the model's maximum sequence length and the
  maximum number of items of each modality allowed, and agree with dummy
  inputs (images/videos) at maximum possible sizes.

       *vllm.multimodal.processing.BaseProcessingInfo.get_supported_mm_limits*
`get_supported_mm_limits()`

Return the maximum supported number of items for each modality.

A value of `None` means unlimited number of items.

Omitting a modality from the returned dictionary means that it is not
supported at all.

      *vllm.multimodal.processing.InputProcessingContext.get_merged_mm_kwargs*
`get_merged_mm_kwargs(kwargs, *, supported_mm_processor_kwargs=None)`

Merge configured and request `mm_processor_kwargs`.

When `supported_mm_processor_kwargs` is provided, flat keys are matched
against the keys supported by each HuggingFace processor kwarg scope.
Matching flat keys are routed to every scope that supports them and removed
from the shared flat namespace; keys not supported by any scope remain flat.

Without `supported_mm_processor_kwargs`, flat keys already represented in at
least one existing mapping-valued scope are removed from the shared flat
namespace; all other flat keys are left unchanged because there is no
information to determine which scopes should receive them.

`PromptInsertion` `dataclass`     *vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptInsertion*

Bases: `PromptUpdate`

Defines how to insert placeholder tokens into a prompt.

Example: For each image, insert a number of `<image>` feature placeholders
equal to the feature size of the vision encoder after the `<s>` token:

>python
    PromptInsertion(
        modality="image",
        target=[bos_token_id],
        insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
    )
<
Insert these tokens at the start of the prompt:

>python
    PromptInsertion(
        modality="image",
        target=PromptIndexTargets.start(),
        insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
    )
<
Insert these tokens after a prefix `Images:`:

>python
    PromptInsertion(
        modality="image",
        target=PromptIndexTargets.prefix(images_prefix_token_ids),
        insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
    )
<
Insert these tokens at the end of the prompt:

>python
    PromptInsertion(
        modality="image",
        target=PromptIndexTargets.end(),
        insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
    )
<
Attributes: ~

- `insertion` (PromptUpdateContent) -- Given the index of the processed item
  within

                        *vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptInsertion.insertion*
`insertion = field(repr=False)` `class-attribute` `instance-attribute`

Given the index of the processed item within
|vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptUpdate.modality|, output the token
sequence to insert right after
|vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptUpdate.target|.

For convenience, you can directly pass in the token sequence instead of a
function if it does not depend on the input.

`PromptReplacement` `dataclass` *vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptReplacement*

Bases: `PromptUpdate`

Defines how to replace portions of an input prompt with placeholder tokens.

Example: For each image, replace one `<image>` input placeholder in the
prompt with a number of `<image>` feature placeholders equal to the feature
size of the vision encoder:

>python
    PromptReplacement(
        modality="image",
        target=[image_token_id],
        replacement=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
    )
<
As above, but further pad the feature placeholders with `<image_bos>` and
`<image_eos>`, which are not supposed to be passed to the vision encoder:

>python
    PromptReplacement(
        modality="image",
        target=[image_token_id],
        replacement=PromptUpdateDetails(
            full=(
                [image_bos_id] + [image_token_id] * image_feature_size + [image_eos_id]
            ),
            is_embed=lambda full: torch.tensor(full) == image_token_id,
        ),
    )
<
Attributes: ~

- `replacement` (PromptUpdateContent) -- Given the index of the processed
  item within

Apply multi-modal prompt updates to token IDs.

*vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor._apply_prompt_updates_via_text*
`_apply_prompt_updates_via_text(token_ids, mm_prompt_updates, *,
    encode_segments_separately=False)`

Apply multi-modal prompt updates in text space, then encode the result.

A non-special-token target may be tokenized differently inside the prompt
because the tokens may go across the boundaries of the target (e.g. when
searching for "foo" in "food", if "food" itself makes up a token, then the
token ID of "foo" will not appear at all). Since it is inefficient to search
for all possible tokenizations of the target in the prompt, we instead
perform text-based updates on the decoded token IDs, then encode them back.

*vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor._get_prompt_updates*
`_get_prompt_updates(mm_items, hf_processor_mm_kwargs, out_mm_kwargs)`
`abstractmethod`

Given the original multi-modal items for this modality and HF-processed
data, output the updates to perform.

The information returned by this method is used to update token inputs which
bypass the HF processor. It is also used to update the output of HF
processor if the HF process does not apply prompt updates to text inputs.

Moreover, this information is critical to determine the token positions in
order to construct |vllm.multimodal.inputs.PlaceholderRange| for each
multi-modal item.

          *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.BaseMultiModalProcessor.apply*
`apply(inputs, timing_ctx)`

Process multi-modal inputs to be used in vLLM.

The main steps are:

1. Perform MM-specific post-processing to the token inputs.
2. Apply HF Processor on multi-modal data together with optional dummy text,
   outputting processed multi-modal data tensors.
3. Find and update sequences in the token IDs with placeholder tokens. The
   number of placeholder tokens equals the feature size of the multi-modal
   data outputted by the multi-modal encoder.
4. Extract information about the placeholder tokens from the processed token
   IDs.

                        *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.PromptInsertion*
`PromptInsertion` `dataclass`

Bases: `PromptUpdate`

Defines how to insert placeholder tokens into a prompt.

Example: For each image, insert a number of `<image>` feature placeholders
equal to the feature size of the vision encoder after the `<s>` token:

>python
    PromptInsertion(
        modality="image",
        target=[bos_token_id],
        insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
    )
<
Insert these tokens at the start of the prompt:

>python
    PromptInsertion(
        modality="image",
        target=PromptIndexTargets.start(),
        insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
    )
<
Insert these tokens after a prefix `Images:`:

>python
    PromptInsertion(
        modality="image",
        target=PromptIndexTargets.prefix(images_prefix_token_ids),
        insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
    )
<
Insert these tokens at the end of the prompt:

>python
    PromptInsertion(
        modality="image",
        target=PromptIndexTargets.end(),
        insertion=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
    )
<
Attributes: ~

- `insertion` (PromptUpdateContent) -- Given the index of the processed item
  within

              *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.PromptInsertion.insertion*
`insertion = field(repr=False)` `class-attribute` `instance-attribute`

|vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptUpdate.modality|, output the token

|vllm.multimodal.processing.PromptUpdate.target|.

                      *vllm.multimodal.processing.processor.PromptReplacement*
`PromptReplacement` `dataclass`

Bases: `PromptUpdate`

Defines how to replace portions of an input prompt with placeholder tokens.

Example: For each image, replace one `<image>` input placeholder in the
prompt with a number of `<image>` feature placeholders equal to the feature
size of the vision encoder:

>python
    PromptReplacement(
        modality="image",
        target=[image_token_id],
        replacement=[image_token_id] * image_feature_size,
    )
<
As above, but further pad the feature placeholders with `<image_bos>` and
`<image_eos>`, which are not supposed to be passed to the vision encoder:

>python
    PromptReplacement(
        modality="image",
        target=[image_token_id],
        replacement=PromptUpdateDetails(
            full=(
                [image_bos_id] + [image_token_id] * image_feature_size + [image_eos_id]
            ),
            is_embed=lambda full: torch.tensor(full) == image_token_id,
        ),
    )
<
Attributes: ~

- `replacement` (PromptUpdateContent) -- Given the index of the processed
  item within

Group consecutive items (possibly from different requests) into batches.

                             *vllm.multimodal.utils.set_mm_embedding_modality*
`set_mm_embedding_modality(embed, modality, placement=None)`

Attach modality metadata to a gathered multimodal embedding tensor.

Used by interleaved Omni merge paths that need to group embeddings by
modality without threading a parallel modalities list through
`embed_input_ids`.

`placement` is `(start, end, is_embed)`: the embedding fills the batch
positions `[start, end)` selected by the CPU mask `is_embed` (all of them if
`None`). It lets models build per-modality position masks without reading
`input_ids` on the host.

                                 *vllm.multimodal.utils.strip_covered_mm_data*
`strip_covered_mm_data(mm_features, num_computed_tokens, uses_mrope=False)`

Drop the tensor data of mm items whose placeholder span is fully inside a
prefix-cache-covered region: no encoder run can be scheduled for them, so
the workers never consume the payload fields. M-RoPE models keep CPU-side
metadata fields used to compute positions. SHM address items are also kept
so workers can balance the sender's reference count. The scheduler-side
`Request` keeps the full features.

`ClefOmniVideoBackend`            *vllm.multimodal.video.ClefOmniVideoBackend*

Bases: `VideoBackend`

Clef-Omni's reference sampling: the first frame at or after each `1/fps`
boundary (frame i sits at `i / original_fps` seconds, so the k-th boundary
is crossed by frame `ceil(k * original_fps / fps)`), capped at 768 frames
and padded to an even count by repeating the last frame.

`DynamicVideoBackend`              *vllm.multimodal.video.DynamicVideoBackend*

Bases: `VideoBackend`

Duration-aware dynamic-sampling video backend.

Samples at `fps` up to `max_duration` seconds, falling back to uniform
sampling across the full duration when the video is longer than
`max_duration`. Codec is selectable the same way as `VideoBackend`.

                           *vllm.multimodal.video.EmbeddingGemma2VideoBackend*
`EmbeddingGemma2VideoBackend`

Bases: `VideoBackend`

Samples frames with the same indices as HF EmbeddingGemma2VideoProcessor.

   *vllm.multimodal.video.EmbeddingGemma2VideoBackend._get_processor_defaults*
`_get_processor_defaults(**kwargs)` `classmethod`

Read default fps and max_frames from video_processor if available.

`GLM46VVideoBackend`                *vllm.multimodal.video.GLM46VVideoBackend*

Bases: `VideoBackend`

GLM-4.6V dynamic FPS video backend.

Faithfully replicates the frame sampling logic from transformers'
`Glm46VVideoProcessor.sample_frames`:

- Dynamic FPS thresholds based on effective video duration:
  `{≤30s: 3fps, ≤300s: 1fps, >300s: 0.5fps}`
- `temporal_patch_size` multiplier (default 2) applied to extract count
- Duration capped at 2400s, frame count capped at 640
- Even frame count enforced (append last frame if odd)

`Glm5NextVideoBackend`            *vllm.multimodal.video.Glm5NextVideoBackend*

Bases: `VideoBackend`

GLM-5.3-Flash fps-interval video backend.

Selects frames with the same sampler the processor falls back to, so only
the sampled frames are materialized. `fps_interval` semantics (default 2.0)
with a temporal-patch-scaled greedy walk, frame count capped at 2048,
temporal pairs kept even. Request overrides: `fps` -> fps interval,
`max_frames` -> frame cap, `temporal_patch_size` (default 2).

            *vllm.multimodal.video.Glm5NextVideoBackend._sample_frame_indices*
`_sample_frame_indices(total_frames, fps, duration, *, target_fps=None,
    max_frame_count=None, temporal_patch_size=2)` `classmethod`

GLM video frame sampling (training-reference parity).

`target_fps` is the `fps_interval` request knob. The greedy walk advances at
`1 / (temporal_patch_size * target_fps)` seconds, so on frame-dense sources
it collects more candidates than `extract_t` and the `> extract_t` fixup
re-spreads the picks uniformly with `np.linspace` -- that fallback is the
intended reference behavior, not an accident. Short clips (fewer frames than
`extract_t`) are spread at evenly spaced timestamps (`floor` sampling; the
linspace variant samples frames unevenly and cost 4 points on video
grounding evals). Request overrides: `target_fps` -> fps interval,
`max_frame_count` -> frame cap.

`Molmo2VideoBackend`                *vllm.multimodal.video.Molmo2VideoBackend*

                            *vllm.multimodal.video.PyNvVideoCodecVideoBackend*
`PyNvVideoCodecVideoBackend`

Bases: `VideoBackend`

Hardware-accelerated video backend using PyNvVideoCodec.

The backend first opens the stream only to read metadata and compute the
sampled frame indices. It then acquires the raw decoded RGB byte count from
the process-local multimodal GPU memory pool before decoding the selected
frames into VRAM. Decoded frames are copied into pinned host memory before
the lease is released, so downstream preprocessing continues to receive a
CPU `np.ndarray` in NHWC RGB format.

`Qwen2VLVideoBackend`              *vllm.multimodal.video.Qwen2VLVideoBackend*

Bases: `VideoBackend`

Qwen2-VL / Qwen2.5-VL fps-based video backend.

Ports transformers' `Qwen2VLVideoProcessor.sample_frames` (fps mode), shared
by Qwen2-VL and Qwen2.5-VL (the latter has no video processor of its own):
sample `total / original_fps * fps` frames, clamp to
`[min_frames, max_frames]` (4 and 768), floor to a multiple of
`temporal_patch_size` (2), and take indices with the exact
`torch.arange(0, total, total / n)` call so they match HF byte-for-byte.

`num_frames` is ignored (fps-driven, like the Qwen3-VL loader). The float32
step can emit an out-of-range tail index (e.g. 451 for a 451-frame clip); it
is clamped to the last valid frame.

`VideoBackend`                            *vllm.multimodal.video.VideoBackend*

Bases: `VideoLoader`

Uniform-sampling video backend.

Samples `num_frames` uniformly across the video (or one frame every `1/fps`
seconds, whichever produces fewer frames). The decoding codec is selected
via the `backend` kwarg (`"opencv"`, `"torchcodec"`, `"pynvvideocodec"`, or
`"deepstream"`), which can be passed through `--media-io-kwargs`. Defaults
to `"opencv"`.

Methods: ~

- `load_bytes` -- Load sampled frames from raw video bytes.

                               *vllm.multimodal.video.VideoBackend.load_bytes*
`load_bytes(data, num_frames=-1, fps=-1, max_duration=300,
    frame_recovery=False, *, backend='opencv', **kwargs)` `classmethod`

Load sampled frames from raw video bytes.

Parameters: ~

- `data` (bytes) -- Raw video bytes.
- `num_frames` (int, default: -1 ) -- Target number of frames to sample (-1
  for all).
- `fps` (int, default: -1 ) -- Target FPS for sampling (-1 for original).
- `max_duration` (int, default: 300 ) -- Maximum duration in seconds ---
  only used by the dynamic subclass; ignored here.
- `frame_recovery` (bool, default: False ) -- Enable forward-scan recovery
  for failed frames. Only honored by the OpenCV codec.
- `backend` (VideoDecoderBackend, default: 'opencv' ) -- Decoding codec ---
  "opencv", "torchcodec", "pynvvideocodec" or "deepstream".
- `kwargs`

  (`Any`, default: `{}` ) --

  Codec-specific options, validated against and forwarded to `backend`:

  - `num_ffmpeg_threads` (TorchCodec): number of FFmpeg decoding threads;
    `0` (default) relies on the FFmpeg default value which is
    `min(cpu_count + 1, 16)`. OpenCV will always use `min(cpu_count, 16)`.
  - `seek_mode` (TorchCodec): `"exact"` (default) guarantees frame-accurate
    sampling by scanning the file on creation, while `"approximate"` skips
    that scan for faster decoder creation at the cost of relying on the
    file's metadata. See
    https://meta-pytorch.org/torchcodec/stable/generated_examples/decoding/approximate_mode.html
    for details.
  - `device` (TorchCodec): `"cpu"` (default) decodes on the host and returns
    a `np.ndarray`; `"cuda"` decodes with NVDEC and returns the frames as a
    CUDA `torch.Tensor`, which a device-side HF video processor can consume
    without a host round-trip.
  - `hw_decoders` (PyNvVideoCodec): maximum number of concurrent decoder
    slots. Defaults to 2 and must be a positive integer.
  - `max_width` / `max_height` (PyNvVideoCodec): optional maximum input
    dimensions configured for each decoder. Both must be positive integers
    and set together. Values are clamped to each codec's hardware limits. By
    default, decoder dimensions also cover the input's opposite orientation
    when that fits the reserved memory and hardware limits.
  - `pool_size` / `timeout_sec` (DeepStream): decoder pool size and pool
    acquisition timeout in seconds.

Returns: ~

- `DecodedFrames` -- Tuple of (frames, metadata_dict), where frames is a
- `dict[str, Any]` -- CPU np.ndarray unless TorchCodec decodes on
  device="cuda".

`SampledFramesCharge`     *vllm.multimodal.video_decoders.SampledFramesCharge*

Charges the decoded size of sampled video frames to a request budget.

`VideoMediaIO` installs one with `charging_sampled_frames` while a loader
runs. Decoders call `charge_sampled_frames` once they know the frame size
and the sampled indices, so an oversized sample is rejected before any frame
is decoded.

`DelegatingParser`                              *vllm.parser.DelegatingParser*

Bases: `Parser`

A Parser implementation that delegates to separate ReasoningParser and
ToolParser instances.

This is the recommended base class for creating model-specific parsers that
combine existing reasoning and tool parser implementations. Subclasses
should set `self._reasoning_parser` and `self._tool_parser` in their
`__init__` method.

If either parser is None, the corresponding methods will return default
values (no reasoning extraction, no tool calls).

                  *vllm.platforms.Platform._align_heterogeneous_kv_block_size*
`_align_heterogeneous_kv_block_size(vllm_config, backend_cls)` `classmethod`

Align block size when several KV dtypes share one block pool.

A quantized primary (e.g. nvfp4) shares the block pool with one or more
higher-precision "padded specs" (skip layers today; the first/last-N sibling
in the future). A padded spec's per-token page is larger than the primary's
and not an integer multiple of it, so the trivial
`unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` cannot reconcile them. We do it here
instead, before the specs are built:

1. Bump the primary `block_size` (kernel-aligned) until the primary page is
   large enough to cover the largest padded-spec page.
2. Record that shared page in each padded spec's `*_page_size_padded` hint,
   so it pads up to the shared page.

`unify` then sees equal pages and stays trivial.

To add a padded-spec type: append its per-token page to `padded_pages` and
set its `*_page_size_padded` hint below.

                            *vllm.platforms.Platform._align_hybrid_block_size*
`_align_hybrid_block_size(vllm_config, backend_cls)` `classmethod`

For hybrid attention/mamba models, ensure that the attention page size is >=
the mamba page size, and pad the mamba page size to match.

                           *vllm.platforms.Platform._check_aligned_block_size*
`_check_aligned_block_size(vllm_config, backend_classes, pre_block_size)`
`classmethod`

Fail now, not at worker setup, if alignment left a rejected size.

Alignment rounds by the first backend's kernel block only, so it can land on
a size a sibling backend rejects.

                              *vllm.platforms.Platform._find_non_ssm_backends*

                  *vllm.platforms.Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends*
`_preferred_block_size_for_backends(backend_classes, default_block_size,
    vllm_config)` `classmethod`

Block size every backend accepts.

One backend keeps its preferred size. When every backend accepts the
default, several backends keep that preference only when they all ask for
the same size and all accept it. Differing preferences keep the default. If
any backend rejects the default, the LCM search is unchanged.

`supports_block_size` may be overridden to accept exact sizes only (CPU_MLA
takes 16 and no multiple of it), so candidates are the LCMs of one supported
size per backend, each checked against every backend.

Raises: ~

- `ValueError` -- If the backends share no supported block size.

                      *vllm.platforms.Platform.apply_config_platform_defaults*
`apply_config_platform_defaults(vllm_config)` `classmethod`

Apply the platform-specific default values to the config.

This function is called during the initialization of global VllmConfig,
after parsing cli arguments. It can modify the defaults of the config
according to the platform. For example, it can enable custom_ops based on
the enabled features.

The config is passed by reference, so it can be modified in place.

layers that share the same layer index (e.g. cross attention and self
attention in the same decoder block of an encoder-decoder model such as
BART).

Platforms that have verified that their `runner_kv_caches` is not impacted
by this case should override this to a no-op. Otherwise the default
implementation raises `NotImplementedError`.

             *vllm.platforms.Platform.device_control_id_to_physical_device_id*
`device_control_id_to_physical_device_id(device_id)` `classmethod`

Map one device-control env entry to an integer physical device ID.

                     *vllm.platforms.Platform.device_id_to_physical_device_id*
`device_id_to_physical_device_id(device_id)` `classmethod`

Map a vLLM-local logical device ID to a physical device ID.

The input is a logical local ID (e.g. a local rank), NOT a visible device
ordinal; for the latter use visible_device_id_to_physical_device_id(). The
two coincide only when no logical-to-physical mapping is in effect.

                     *vllm.platforms.Platform.get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls*
`get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls(vllm_config)` `classmethod`

Resolve the fully-qualified class path of the platform's KV cache config
builder.

  Note: ~

  Experimental, like the `KVCacheConfigBuilder` interface it selects.

The builder supplies grouping (`get_kv_cache_groups`) and tensor placement
(`get_kv_cache_config_from_groups`). Vendors may override this to return a
platform-specific builder. The default builder honors a model implementing
`SupportsKVCacheGrouping`; a builder that overrides `get_kv_cache_groups`
owns grouping and bypasses that model hook unless it calls `super()`.

Returns: ~

- `str` -- Fully-qualified class path of a KVCacheConfigBuilder subclass.

                         *vllm.platforms.Platform.get_mla_prefill_backend_cls*

return it directly. The default implementation selects the best backend from
a device-capability-based priority list.

Returns: ~

- `type[MLAPrefillBackend]` -- The selected backend class.

Raises: ~

- `ValueError` -- If no MLA prefill backend is valid for the configuration.

                         *vllm.platforms.Platform.is_device_capability_family*
`is_device_capability_family(capability, device_id=0)` `classmethod`

Returns True if the device capability is any .x. Mirrors CUDA 13 'family'
architecture semantics (e.g. 10.x, 11.x, 12.x).

`is_fp8_fnuz()` `classmethod`            *vllm.platforms.Platform.is_fp8_fnuz*

Returns whether the preferred FP8 type is FNUZ on the current platform.

There are two representations of FP8, OCP FP8 and FNUZ FP8. The OCP
specification can be found at https://tinyurl.com/b7jvwpft. The FNUZ
specification can be found at https://tinyurl.com/5n6hwwu5.

AMD's MI300 and MI325 have native hardware support for FNUZ. All other
hardware has converged on the OCP FP8 standard.

                                   *vllm.platforms.Platform.is_integrated_gpu*
`is_integrated_gpu(device_id=0)` `classmethod`

Returns whether the GPU is an integrated (UMA) device that shares system
memory with the CPU. device_id None means the current device.

On UMA systems (e.g. NVIDIA GH200, DGX Spark, Jetson Orin), cudaMemGetInfo
may underreport free memory because it does not account for reclaimable OS
memory (page cache, buffers).

              *vllm.platforms.Platform.logical_device_id_to_visible_device_id*
`logical_device_id_to_visible_device_id(device_id)` `classmethod`

Map a vLLM-local logical device ID to the current process's visible
accelerator ordinal.

vLLM internals use logical local IDs. Physical IDs are used only at
platform/topology boundaries. This helper performs the final translation
needed by APIs such as `torch.device("cuda:N")`.

the old pool allocated, and capturing into it would fail.

        *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform._align_heterogeneous_kv_block_size*
`_align_heterogeneous_kv_block_size(vllm_config, backend_cls)` `classmethod`

Align block size when several KV dtypes share one block pool.

A quantized primary (e.g. nvfp4) shares the block pool with one or more
higher-precision "padded specs" (skip layers today; the first/last-N sibling
in the future). A padded spec's per-token page is larger than the primary's
and not an integer multiple of it, so the trivial
`unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` cannot reconcile them. We do it here
instead, before the specs are built:

1. Bump the primary `block_size` (kernel-aligned) until the primary page is
   large enough to cover the largest padded-spec page.
2. Record that shared page in each padded spec's `*_page_size_padded` hint,
   so it pads up to the shared page.

`unify` then sees equal pages and stays trivial.

To add a padded-spec type: append its per-token page to `padded_pages` and
set its `*_page_size_padded` hint below.

                  *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform._align_hybrid_block_size*
`_align_hybrid_block_size(vllm_config, backend_cls)` `classmethod`

For hybrid attention/mamba models, ensure that the attention page size is >=
the mamba page size, and pad the mamba page size to match.

                 *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform._check_aligned_block_size*
`_check_aligned_block_size(vllm_config, backend_classes, pre_block_size)`
`classmethod`

Fail now, not at worker setup, if alignment left a rejected size.

Alignment rounds by the first backend's kernel block only, so it can land on
a size a sibling backend rejects.

                    *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform._find_non_ssm_backends*

        *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends*
`_preferred_block_size_for_backends(backend_classes, default_block_size,
    vllm_config)` `classmethod`

Block size every backend accepts.

One backend keeps its preferred size. When every backend accepts the
default, several backends keep that preference only when they all ask for
the same size and all accept it. Differing preferences keep the default. If
any backend rejects the default, the LCM search is unchanged.

`supports_block_size` may be overridden to accept exact sizes only (CPU_MLA
takes 16 and no multiple of it), so candidates are the LCMs of one supported
size per backend, each checked against every backend.

Raises: ~

- `ValueError` -- If the backends share no supported block size.

`is_fp8_fnuz()` `classmethod`  *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform.is_fp8_fnuz*

Returns whether the preferred FP8 type is FNUZ on the current platform.

There are two representations of FP8, OCP FP8 and FNUZ FP8. The OCP
specification can be found at https://tinyurl.com/b7jvwpft. The FNUZ
specification can be found at https://tinyurl.com/5n6hwwu5.

AMD's MI300 and MI325 have native hardware support for FNUZ. All other
hardware has converged on the OCP FP8 standard.

                         *vllm.platforms.interface.Platform.is_integrated_gpu*

Returns whether the GPU is an integrated (UMA) device that shares system
memory with the CPU. device_id None means the current device.

On UMA systems (e.g. NVIDIA GH200, DGX Spark, Jetson Orin), cudaMemGetInfo
may underreport free memory because it does not account for reclaimable OS
memory (page cache, buffers).
